18397-socialism-and-modern-science-darwi:
Enrico Ferri wrote this study of socialism and modern science, subtitled Darwin, Spencer, Marx, translated by Robert Rives La Monte and published in Chicago by Charles H. Kerr in a third edition in 1917, with copyright in 1900. Ferri asks whether Darwin's theory of evolution supports or contradicts socialism, a question debated hotly at the Congress of Munich by Virchow and Haeckel.

Contents treat three alleged contradictions between Darwinism and socialism: the equality of individuals, the struggle for life and its victims, and the survival of the fittest. Ferri then presents socialism as a consequence of Darwinism, treating religious belief, the individual and the species, and the struggle for life against the class struggle. Readers get a socialist classic of science: evolution read as the ground of collective action, not of mere competition.
37290-the-life-and-teaching-of-karl-marx:
The Life and Teaching of Karl Marx is a life and creed book by Beer. Two men turned it to English, and Beer checked the turn with his own hand. A Labour Press house of London first brought it out in nineteen twenty one. Front parts weigh what Marx means and what Hegel left to him. Youth, school years, and first print steps fill the next part rank.

Friend link with Engels and fights with Bauer and Proudhon mark his growth years. The joint creed sheet of eighteen forty eight stands in the stir years part. London cloud and sun days, the world work band, and the Paris Commune fill mid parts. Wealth creed, class war, and the work host role fill the creed scheme. Land rule creed of the past heads that creed part in the list.
39653-historical-materialism-and-the-eco:
Benedetto Croce wrote Historical Materialism and the Economics of Karl Marx, essays on a famed doctrine. C M Meredith turned the book into English for its press. George Allen and Unwin issued it in London in nineteen hundred fifteen. A D Lindsay of Balliol College, Oxford, wrote its front note.

Croce takes Labriola’s book as his launch point in chapter one. The doctrine is no scheme of all past time, he argues there. Nor is it a new way of writing the past at all. Fresh facts, not fresh method, are its true gift to study. Cash wants have swayed great deeds far more than men saw. That sway is its one sound claim on our heed, Croce holds. He denies that all past time is cash time in disguise. Right and wrong still stand on their own feet in his close.
48446-karl-marx:
Achille Loria wrote Karl Marx, a sketch, Englished from the Italian and printed in New York in 1920. Eden and Cedar Paul made the rendering and wrote a foreword. Their note holds that the social teaching that stirs hopes and fears to-day is of the school of Marx. No one much fears, or troubles to answer, any other school that takes the name. The first chapter opens on a puzzle of the garden of human thought.

Rebel blossoms, Loria writes, so often spring from seeds of the high-born. The most fiery spirits emerge from homes of reaction. Looked at closely, the thing is less strange. Only those who live in a given world can fully grasp its faults. So it was with the great rebels: Dante, Voltaire, Byron, Kropotkin, and Tolstoi, all born to property. Like was the lot of Karl Marx.
60412-rx:
Rx is a science fiction story by Alan Nourse, first printed in Worlds of If in October 1957. A headnote sets the case. The tenth son of a tenth son was very sick, but it was written that he would never die. It was up to the Earth doctor to see that he did not.

A crash priority call comes in from Morua the Second, and Red Doctor Sam Jenkins swings the patrol ship Lancet toward it. Then the survey card shows a black stripe. Morua is a class six planet, a plague spot that has thrown out five Earth missions. It shot half of one crew and cut the ears off the rest. Green Doctor Wally Stone wants to file a protest, but the law demands instant response.
socialism-and-modern-science-darwin-spen: Enrico Ferri wrote Socialism and Modern Science. Robert Rives La Monte turned the book into English. The third edition came out at Chicago in 1917. Charles H. Kerr and Company printed it. The work rests on a 1900 copyright. The contents open with a preface and a first part. That part treats three claimed clashes between Darwinism and socialism. It names Virchow and Haeckel at the Munich congress. It then takes up the equality of persons. The struggle for life and the survival of the fittest follow.
